Coast Notes / GOLD COAST

Maintaining outdoor dining areas.

We scope paving, entrances, fixed items and drainage with the way your outdoor venue works, including customer routes and reopening conditions.

Start reading ↓
In this article

Decide whether the surface or the water route needs work.

An outdoor dining area is an occupied working space. Tables move, deliveries pass through and water follows the available surface and drainage route. We review the physical defect alongside that use, so the proposal explains both the repair and the part of the venue affected while it is carried out.

Read the space before defining the repair

Photograph paving, thresholds, fittings and outlets alongside customer, table and delivery routes. Include adjacent surfaces when recording pooling or movement.

The history matters: whether water appears after washing or rain, whether the same area settles again and whether an earlier repair changed the surface. These observations help us decide which parts of the accessible route and substrate need further assessment.

Where water remains near planters or low door thresholds, note the surface fall and whether it follows rain, washing or a blocked outlet. Cleaning can remove debris, but re-seating loose paving or correcting drainage calls for a separate work scope. Mark how furniture, deliveries and customers will move before agreeing barriers.

Restaurants & cafés ↗
02

Choose the work that fits the condition

Record rainfall and cleaning water separately. Check each source and outlet before defining cleaning, local adjustment or drainage inspection.

A floor that is slippery during service may have cleaning residue or tracked-in material. Water that returns to the same spot after rain points to the inlet, falls or paving base. Dry-weather wetting warrants a look at nearby irrigation and washdown use. We define the cleaning and runoff plan separately from resetting pavers, repairing a base or changing a drainage detail, then agree when tables and customers can return.

  • Cleaning

    Confirm surface, cleaning method, protection and water handling. Record defects revealed after cleaning as separate repairs.

  • Local repair

    The repair area includes the affected material, the support or preparation required and the finish at the adjoining edge. Matching is considered before replacement materials are agreed.

  • A wider change

    Where the findings support drainage or surface alterations, we separate investigation, design or approval information needed and the physical work to be quoted.

Restaurants & cafés ↗

Confirm whether the area is public or private

Observe the paving during a rain event and during normal cleaning. Note where runoff collects and whether the low point lies on the staff route or beside a table, then choose a suitable work window.

Gold Coast roadside-dining requirements address dining on public land, including the layout and pedestrian space. We ask for the relevant approved arrangement when that setting applies, so work boundaries and temporary furniture movement can be considered against it.

A private terrace, shared forecourt or leased outdoor area has its own property arrangements. We confirm the nominated contact and work boundary rather than assuming that every café terrace follows the same approval conditions.

Sequence the work around the venue

  1. 01

    Agree the released zone

    Tables, planters, deliveries and the customer route are reviewed with your manager before the area is made available.

  2. 02

    Prepare, repair and clean

    The agreed method includes protection, removal or preparation, repair materials and waste handling. Cleaning runoff is managed as part of the work.

  3. 03

    Confirm return-to-use conditions

    The material, completed work and intended use determine reopening. We record any drying, curing, checking or follow-up requirement affecting the area.

Keep the quotation and handover specific

Area, depth, substrate work, material matching, drainage investigation, restricted access and repeated attendance can change the scope. We identify these factors before agreeing the work, together with the protection and waste arrangements.

The handover records the areas treated, repairs completed, actual checks and any outstanding item. Where the original issue was recurring water, the agreed observation or further action stays linked to the initial report.

Set aside time for material curing and cleaning. Agree how furniture and surrounding finishes will be protected, where waste will go, and how cleaning wastewater will be contained.

Agree the conditions for reopening.

Check public-land arrangements where applicable and list curing, cleaning and runoff protection before reopening.

  • Puddles and damaged paving
  • Trading and pedestrian route
  • Cure and clean-up check

Common questions

Does cleaning a terrace solve recurring ponding?
Cleaning addresses surface build-up. When the same spot ponds after rain, we check the inlet, falls and paving base before deciding on clearing, resetting paving or drainage work.
Can pressure washing solve a recurring drainage problem?
We assess the surface and accessible water route first. Cleaning is scoped for suitable surfaces and deposits; damaged paving, underlying movement or a downstream issue needs its own assessment and work.
